title: Lab Practical 1 – Foundations & Integument
notes: Identify anatomical position, body regions, directional terms, and planes on models.
Locate major body cavities and associated serous membranes (pleura, pericardium, peritoneum).
Distinguish epithelial tissues by layers and cell shape (simple vs stratified; squamous, cuboidal, columnar).
Identify connective tissue types by matrix and fibers (areolar, adipose, dense regular/irregular, hyaline cartilage).
Recognize muscle tissues (skeletal striations, cardiac intercalated discs, smooth spindle cells).
Recognize nervous tissue (neurons vs neuroglia; cell body, axon, dendrites).
Integument: identify layers (epidermis strata), hair follicle, sebaceous and sweat glands.
Use skeleton list to locate key bones and markings (e.g., femur head/neck, humerus greater tubercle, skull sutures).
Practice labeling abdominopelvic regions and quadrants for organ location questions.
Memorize ABCDE criteria for melanoma for applied questions.
Be ready to identify tissue slides at low/high magnification by hallmark features.
Know serous membrane names per cavity and organ (visceral vs parietal).
Differentiate thick vs thin skin histologically (presence of stratum lucidum).
Understand bone tissue histology (osteons vs trabeculae) for ID items.
Directional terms applied to limbs (proximal/distal) vs trunk (superior/inferior).
Common traps: confusing simple cuboidal with stratified cuboidal (rare); check nuclei layers.
Identify dermal papillae (fingerprints) and associated receptors.
Skeleton landmarks from the provided list are high-yield—drill articulations and foramina.
Use weekly objectives as a checklist for lab preps.
Expect practical stations with images/models; time management matters—scan hallmarks first.

questions.question: Which feature identifies cardiac muscle on a slide?
questions.explanation: Cardiac muscle is striated with intercalated discs.

questions.question: Simple squamous epithelium is best for:
questions.explanation: Thin, flat cells permit rapid diffusion.

questions.question: Thick skin contains which extra layer?
questions.explanation: Stratum lucidum is present in thick skin.

questions.question: In compact bone, the central (Haversian) canal contains:
questions.explanation: Nerves and blood vessels run centrally.
